subject: science
intro: Energy cannot be created or destroyed, only transferred or changed from one form to another. This is the law of conservation of energy. In a system, if energy leaves one part, the same amount of energy goes into other parts, so the total energy stays the same. Two common forms are kinetic energy (energy of motion) and potential energy (stored energy, such as from height). When a ball falls, its stored potential energy changes into kinetic energy, but the total energy is conserved.

items.prompt: A falling ball loses 20 joules of potential energy. If no energy is lost to the air, how much kinetic energy does it gain?

steps: Energy is conserved, so the lost potential energy goes into kinetic energy.
The ball loses 20 joules of potential energy.
So it gains 20 joules of kinetic energy.
solution.answer: 20 joules, because the lost potential energy is conserved as kinetic energy.

items.prompt: What does the law of conservation of energy state?

steps: Energy behaves in a specific way in any system.
It cannot be created or destroyed, only transferred or changed in form.
So the total energy of a system stays the same.
solution.answer: Energy cannot be created or destroyed, only transferred or changed, so the total energy stays the same.

items.prompt: In a system, one part gains 15 joules of energy. If the total energy is conserved, how much energy did the rest of the system lose?

steps: Conservation of energy means the total stays the same.
If one part gained 15 joules, that energy came from the rest of the system.
So the rest of the system lost 15 joules.
solution.answer: 15 joules, because the energy gained by one part was lost by the rest (total is conserved).

items.prompt: Name the form of energy an object has because it is moving.

steps: The energy of motion is kinetic energy.

items.prompt: A swinging pendulum is highest (most stored energy) at the ends and fastest at the bottom. Explain the energy change using conservation.

steps: At the ends, the pendulum is high and still, so it has the most potential (stored) energy.
At the bottom, it is low and fast, so the stored energy has changed into kinetic energy.
Energy is conserved: potential energy converts to kinetic and back, keeping the total the same.
solution.answer: Potential energy at the top changes to kinetic energy at the bottom and back, with the total energy conserved.

items.prompt: A 30 joule system transfers 10 joules from a hot block to a cold block. Use conservation to find the energy change of each block.

steps: Conservation means the energy lost by one equals the energy gained by the other.
So the cold block gains 10 joules, and the total energy stays 30 joules.
solution.answer: The hot block loses 10 joules and the cold block gains 10 joules, so the total stays 30 joules.
